normative_extracts.spec_section: Streams Living Standard §6 Queuing Strategies & Backpressure
normative_extracts.quote: Backpressure is the mechanism by which a consumer signals to a producer to slow down when the internal queue's desiredSize drops to zero or below.

engine_internals.mechanism_summary: Each stream tracks queued bytes against highWaterMark; when desiredSize <= 0, pull() stops firing upstream until the consumer drains chunks.

production_failures.symptom: Browser tab OOMs when streaming a 1.5 GB file through a custom TransformStream
production_failures.root_cause: Default CountQueuingStrategy({ highWaterMark: 1 }) counts chunks, not bytes, or producer ignores controller.desiredSize <= 0 and pushes unboundedly.
production_failures.mitigation: Use ByteLengthQueuingStrategy({ highWaterMark: 65536 }) and honor controller.desiredSize or pipeTo() instead of manual enqueue loops.

production_failures.symptom: TypeError: ReadableStream is locked when reading response.body twice
production_failures.root_cause: A ReadableStream allows only one active reader at a time; calling getReader() or response.json() locks the stream.
production_failures.mitigation: Use response.clone() before reading or stream.tee() when two consumers must inspect the same bytes.
